source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The corrected-posterior theorem uses smooth propensity dependence and pointwise-Lipschitz influence-function control; the authors identify these as sufficient conditions and cover smooth incremental interventions.
The cited article studies the value of a possibly non-unique optimal treatment strategy and gives its exceptional-law regularity characterization.
The paper defines incremental propensity-score interventions through odds multiplication, derives efficiency theory, and emphasizes absence of a positivity requirement.
The paper establishes a Bayesian-bootstrap corrected-posterior framework with high-level no-bias, stability, and empirical-process requirements.
The result concerns sup-norm contraction of random dyadic density histograms over Hölder classes, not joint treatment/outcome conditional-coordinate contraction.
The paper develops influence-function inference for nonsmooth IV causal-bound functionals under a novel margin condition; it is not a capped propensity-policy result.
The paper provides plug-in classifier fast rates under a margin assumption and matching classification lower-bound constructions.
The article establishes a double-robust Bayesian procedure and asymptotically exact ATE credible-set coverage under unconfoundedness.
The article connects nondifferentiability in local experiments to restrictions on regular estimation; it does not provide this policy-specific tangent construction.
The paper treats inference for directionally differentiable maps and derivative-bootstrap repairs, without deriving the capped-policy conditional modulus requested here.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Extend the histogram BvM from the fixed uniform/identity benchmark to a scalar design with density bounded above and below and a monotone propensity with controlled endpoint behavior, retaining a fully explicit random-arm-count argument.
Sharpen the local-inference OEQ by specifying a finite active-cell experiment, its loss criterion, and the conditional-modulus optimization domain before attempting the general local result.

Add Díaz–van der Laan-style stochastic-intervention and conditional incremental-effect references to make the policy-survey boundary more complete, while preserving the distinction between hard probability capping and smooth odds shifts.
